messages.author: bebd85531a67ef86
messages.subject: Error: object 'sampler_RW_FooBar' not found
parts:
Hi

Let's say I've written an MCMC sampler called sampler_RW_FooBar and I've put the code in two different files. 

The first file is ~/nimbleProject/nimble/packages/nimble/R/MCMC_samplers.R, which is a local version of a fork of devel at https://github.com/nimble-dev/nimble

The second file is in some other directory that is not associated with that fork.

In emacs (with ESS installed), if I highlight the code for sampler_RW_FooBar,  send it to a new R terminal (after doing 'library(nimble)' of course) and then type 'sampler_RW_FooBar' in the R terminal, I get two different results depending on which file I did this from.

From the first (fork associated) file, R returns the message "Error: object 'sampler_RW_FooBar' not found".

From the second (independent) file everything works as expected and I can use buildMCMC etc etc with the new sampler.

Additionally, if I reinstall nimble using my forked version, then sampler_RW_FooBar becomes available as soon as I do 'library(nimble'). So the issue is entirely about sending code from the forked directory tree to the R terminal.

Right now, my only work around is develop in the second file and transfer the code to the first at appropriate moments. But this seems redundant. I wonder if anyone else has come across this and whether there is a known work around.

David

messages.author: bebd85531a67ef86
messages.subject: Re: Error: object 'sampler_RW_FooBar' not found
parts:
Many thanks for your reply Chris.  

The bad news is I've not been able to reproduce exactly the same behavior - although I can reproduce something not completely dissimilar and quite disturbing.

I don't know if you use emacs (just in case, C=control key, M=Alt key). With the package Emacs Speaks Statistics (ESS) I typically open an R session in an emacs "buffer" (~=a window) in one of three ways: (a) M-x R starts a new R buffer (b) C-c C-n sends a line from an R script to an R buffer, creating a new one if none exist (c) C-c C-s permits to switch the R buffer associated with a script or to create a new R buffer. 

To send code from an R script to an R buffer I most typically use (1) C-c C-n, sends one line & steps (2) C-c M-r, sends a highlighted region. Another option (3) is a much longer copy and paste, i.e. highlight the code, M-w (copy), switch to the R buffer, C-y (paste).

The funny thing is, I get different results depending on if I use method (2) or method (3).

First, if working from a script in the forked code...
After method (2), typing 'sampler_RW_FooBar' in the R buffer results in the function being printed with the final line 

<environment: namespace:nimble>

Whereas after method (3), the final line prints like this...

<environment: 0x5211ca8>

So curiously the two methods result in the code going to two different environments.


Now, working from a script that is not in a directory of the forked code...
Method (2), typing 'sampler_RW_FooBar' in the R buffer results in the function being printed with the final line 
<environment: 0x4497260>
Whereas after method (3), the final line prints like this...
<environment: 0x5cfbdc8>

The environment ID numbers are unique each time you do these steps. So my layman's interpretation is that each time I do these steps the function is redefined in R and a unique environment is created for the obects within the funciton. Now for some reason, using the C-c M-r  (method (2)) approach the unique environment is not established and nimble's addSampler function returns an error

> mcmcConf$addSampler('y', type="RW_FooBar")
Error in mcmcConf$addSampler("y", type = "RW_FooBar") : 
  cannot find sampler type 'RW_FooBar'

If I send 'a <- 5' via method (2) from a file in the forked directory tree and the type 'a' in the R terminal it finds it.

So to conclude: 
Method 2 (the fastest method I use), when used from the forked directory tree, fails to set up an environment for the function resulting in addSampler not finding sampler_RW_FooBar.
Method 3 is slower, clunkier and less ideal, but an environment is correctly assigned and addSampler can find sampler_RW_FooBar

So I'm curious what it is about this combination of git, nimble, emacs and R that results in method 2  (from the forked directory tree only) failing to do the right thing in setting up the function's environment and how that could be fixed?

David

messages.author: bebd85531a67ef86
messages.subject: Re: Error: object 'sampler_RW_FooBar' not found
parts:
It's a complete hack, but here's an emacs macro that enables sending a whole nimble function to the latest R buffer without using ESS and avoiding the environment / namespace problem. Perhaps this is useful to someone. 

;; Copies a nimbleFunction to most recently used R buffer (avoiding ESS)
(fset 'nimbleFunction2R
   [?\C-r ?n ?i ?m ?b ?l ?e ?F ?u ?n ?c ?t ?i ?o ?n left home ?\C-  end home ?\C-s ?\( left ?\C-\M-n ?\M-w ?\C-c ?\C-z ?\C-x ?\] ?\C-y return])

So now 'M-x nim tab enter' provides a pretty rapid alternative to using ESS.
